description: The Antilla wreck is one of Aruba’s signature wreck dives, with a large hull that has become a marine habitat off the island’s northwest coast.
The Great Blue Hole is a circular marine sinkhole at Lighthouse Reef. Its dramatic geology makes it one of Belize’s most recognizable underwater landmarks.
Half Moon Caye Wall combines a reef wall with the offshore setting of Lighthouse Reef, close to Belize’s protected Half Moon Caye.
1000 Steps is a signature Bonaire shore dive, named for the limestone staircase leading down to the beach and reef.
The Hilma Hooker is Bonaire’s best-known wreck dive, resting beside the reef on the island’s sheltered western coast.
Salt Pier is a distinctive Bonaire dive beneath the island’s salt-loading structure, where submerged pilings provide habitat for reef fish.
Bloody Bay Wall is a signature Little Cayman dive, known for the sharp transition from shallow reef to a deep underwater wall.
Babylon is a Grand Cayman wall dive with coral-covered formations along the island’s northern reef system.
Stingray City is Grand Cayman’s famous stingray encounter site in North Sound. The area includes distinct shallow-water and scuba experiences.
The former USS Kittiwake is an intentionally sunk rescue ship off Grand Cayman, now a prominent artificial reef and wreck dive.
The Superior Producer is a cargo-ship wreck near Willemstad. Its recognizable hull makes it one of Curaçao’s signature wreck sites.
Tugboat is a small wreck close to shore in Curaçao, combining a recognizable boat with surrounding reef habitat.
The RMS Rhone is a historic shipwreck near Salt Island, with separate wreck sections spread across the seabed.
Chikuzen is a large refrigerated cargo-ship wreck away from the main islands, offering an offshore wreck experience in the British Virgin Islands.
Tiger Beach is a renowned shark-diving area off Grand Bahama, associated with sandy seabeds and specialist shark encounters.
Dean’s Blue Hole is a deep marine sinkhole beside Long Island. Its sheltered-looking surface contrasts with the dramatic underwater drop.
Half Moon Bay Wall is part of Roatán’s reef system near West End, combining reef scenery with the island’s characteristic drop-offs.
Scotts Head Drop Off lies near Dominica’s southern tip, where the island’s volcanic underwater terrain forms steep reef slopes.
Darwin’s Arch, now known for its remaining pillars, marks an iconic offshore Galápagos diving area associated with large marine animals.
Gordon Rocks is a volcanic formation near Santa Cruz in the Galápagos, renowned for open-water diving and hammerhead shark encounters.
Kicker Rock rises dramatically from the ocean near San Cristóbal. Its submerged walls and channel form a signature Galápagos dive.
Bajo Alcyone is an offshore underwater seamount at Cocos Island, celebrated for pelagic marine life and schooling hammerhead sharks.
Dirty Rock is a signature Cocos Island dive around exposed rock formations, with surrounding waters associated with schooling sharks.
Roca Partida is a remote volcanic pinnacle in the Revillagigedo archipelago, with near-vertical underwater walls and pelagic marine life.
Cenote Dos Ojos is a celebrated freshwater cavern system near Tulum, with limestone formations and clear-water passages explored on guided cavern dives.
Palancar Gardens is part of Cozumel’s Palancar reef system, known for coral formations and the island’s characteristic drift-diving environment.
The Spiegel Grove is a large former naval ship sunk off Key Largo, forming one of the Florida Keys’ landmark artificial reefs.
Blue Heron Bridge is a celebrated shore-diving site in Riviera Beach, Florida, valued for small marine life around the bridge and surrounding seabed.
Silfra is a freshwater fissure in Þingvellir National Park, famous for clear water and the exposed geology of Iceland’s rift landscape.
Scapa Flow is a historic wreck-diving destination in Orkney, best known for the remains of the scuttled German High Seas Fleet.
HMS Scylla is a former naval frigate intentionally sunk near Plymouth, creating a prominent artificial reef off England’s southwest coast.
The Farne Islands are a Northumberland diving destination associated with grey seals, rocky underwater terrain and cold-water marine life.
The Zenobia is a large roll-on, roll-off ferry wreck near Larnaca, one of the Mediterranean’s most recognizable shipwreck dives.
The Blue Hole at Dwejra is a natural limestone entry pool on Gozo, opening into the surrounding Mediterranean reef landscape.
Gozo’s Inland Sea connects a sheltered lagoon to the open Mediterranean through a natural rock tunnel at Dwejra.
Um El Faroud is a former tanker intentionally sunk off Malta, now a major artificial reef and wreck-diving landmark.
El Bajón is a volcanic underwater formation off La Restinga on El Hierro, a signature site in the Canary Islands.
Princess Alice Bank is an offshore seamount in the Azores, known as an open-ocean diving destination associated with mobula rays.
The SS Thistlegorm is a Second World War cargo-ship wreck in the northern Red Sea, famous for its surviving vehicles and cargo.
Shark and Yolanda Reef is a signature Ras Mohammed dive, combining dramatic reef walls with the scattered remains of the Yolanda wreck’s cargo.
Elphinstone is an offshore reef near Marsa Alam, recognized for its elongated shape, steep walls and northern and southern plateaus.
Daedalus Reef is an isolated Red Sea reef marked by a lighthouse, surrounded by steep walls and open-water marine habitat.
Jackson Reef is one of the Straits of Tiran’s landmark reefs, with coral-covered slopes beside deep-water channels.
Dahab’s Blue Hole is a coastal sinkhole beside the Gulf of Aqaba, with a distinct reef opening and deep underwater terrain.
The Canyon near Dahab is a distinctive fissure in the reef, recognized for its narrow rock formations and surrounding coral habitat.
Big Brother Island is a remote Red Sea reef and lighthouse island, known for walls and the Numidia and Aida shipwrecks.
Aliwal Shoal is an offshore reef system near Umkomaas, known for rocky reef habitat and seasonal ragged-tooth shark encounters.
Protea Banks’ Northern Shark Caves form part of an offshore reef system near Shelly Beach, a renowned South African shark-diving area.
Two Mile Reef is a signature Sodwana Bay reef, with varied coral formations along South Africa’s subtropical coastline.
Manta Reef is a well-known Tofo dive, associated with reef formations and cleaning-station habitat used by manta rays.
Japanese Garden is a signature Aqaba reef dive, with coral habitat along Jordan’s short Red Sea coastline.
Two Mile Reef lies in the Bazaruto area, where coral reef habitat sits among Mozambique’s offshore islands and sandy shallows.
Maaya Thila is a celebrated underwater pinnacle in North Ari Atoll, with reef ledges and an established reputation for night diving.
Fish Head is a signature Ari Atoll thila, with steep reef sides and overhangs supporting a variety of reef fish.
Maalhos Thila is an Ari Atoll reef pinnacle known for its overhangs and soft-coral scenery.
Kandooma Thila is an underwater reef formation in South Malé Atoll, associated with channel diving and pelagic marine life.
Miyaru Kandu is a channel dive in Vaavu Atoll, where reef edges meet the deeper waters outside the atoll.
Alimatha’s house reef is a signature Vaavu Atoll site, particularly associated with evening dives and nurse shark encounters.
Cape Kri is a Raja Ampat reef point near Kri Island, celebrated for its diversity of reef fish and surrounding coral habitat.
Melissa’s Garden is a signature Raja Ampat coral garden in the Fam Islands, known for extensive hard-coral formations.
Blue Magic is an offshore Raja Ampat reef near the Dampier Strait, associated with schooling fish and visits from larger marine animals.
Manta Sandy is a Raja Ampat cleaning-station site, where a sandy seabed and reef features provide habitat used by manta rays.
Boo Windows is a Misool dive in southern Raja Ampat, named for openings in the rock formations near the waterline.
Batu Bolong is an isolated rock and reef in Komodo National Park, known for dense coral growth and surrounding marine life.
Castle Rock is a submerged reef formation in northern Komodo, recognized for schooling fish and its open-water setting.
Crystal Rock is a signature northern Komodo reef, with a rock pinnacle and coral-covered slopes in the surrounding channels.
The Cauldron is a channel site in northern Komodo, known for sculpted underwater terrain between neighboring islands.
Cannibal Rock is a southern Komodo underwater pinnacle, valued for colorful invertebrates and reef life around its rocky slopes.
The USAT Liberty is a historic shipwreck beside Tulamben’s shore in Bali, with coral-covered wreckage spread across a sloping seabed.
Crystal Bay is a sheltered-looking bay on Nusa Penida with a reef opening to deeper water, associated with seasonal ocean sunfish encounters.
Nudi Falls is a signature Lembeh Strait site, known for small marine creatures around a sloping seabed and reef habitat.
Barracuda Point is a signature Sipadan dive, where reef slopes meet deeper water and large schools of fish gather.
South Point lies at Sipadan’s southern end, with reef walls and open-water habitat associated with larger marine animals.
Richelieu Rock is an isolated reef in the Andaman Sea, celebrated for colorful reef life and occasional whale shark encounters.
Sail Rock rises between Koh Tao and Koh Phangan, with submerged rock faces and a distinctive vertical chimney formation.
Chumphon Pinnacle is an offshore Koh Tao dive, with submerged granite formations supporting anemones and schooling fish.
Elephant Head Rock is a signature Similan Islands dive, named for granite formations above and below the water.
Koh Bon is an Andaman Sea island dive, recognized for its submerged ridge and association with manta ray encounters.
Bida Nok is a limestone island near Phi Phi, with reef slopes and rock walls supporting varied Andaman Sea marine life.
Kimud Shoal is an offshore dive near Malapascua, especially associated with encounters with thresher sharks.
Monad Shoal is an offshore seamount near Malapascua, internationally known for its connection with thresher shark diving.
Apo Island is a celebrated reef-diving destination near Dauin, known for its community marine sanctuary and coral habitat.
The Canyons is a signature Puerto Galera dive, with underwater channels and rock formations along the Verde Island Passage.
Blue Corner is a signature Palau reef point, renowned for schooling fish, sharks and its position beside deep ocean water.
Ulong Channel is a reef channel in Palau, with coral habitat along its edges and a sandy passage through the reef.
Blue Holes is a group of openings in Palau’s reef that lead into a large underwater cavern near Blue Corner.
Chandelier Cave is a Palau cavern system named for limestone formations in its chambers near Koror.
Fujikawa Maru is a signature Second World War wreck in Chuuk Lagoon, known for surviving aircraft-related cargo and coral-covered structures.
Shinkoku Maru is a large Second World War tanker wreck in Chuuk Lagoon, with extensive structures now colonized by marine life.
Tiputa Pass connects Rangiroa’s lagoon to the open ocean, creating a signature Tuamotu diving area associated with dolphins and sharks.
The Great White Wall is a signature Rainbow Reef dive in the Somosomo Strait, named for its pale soft-coral-covered reef face.
Shark Reef Marine Reserve is a celebrated Beqa-area diving site, associated with organized shark encounters off Fiji’s main island.
The SS President Coolidge is a large wartime troopship wreck near Luganville, one of Vanuatu’s signature dive attractions.
Million Dollar Point is a historic underwater equipment site near Luganville, where discarded wartime machinery forms an unusual marine habitat.
The SS Yongala is a historic shipwreck off Queensland, renowned for the concentration of marine life around its isolated hull.
Cod Hole is a signature Ribbon Reefs dive on the Great Barrier Reef, particularly associated with large potato cod.
Steve’s Bommie is a distinct coral pinnacle on the Great Barrier Reef’s Ribbon Reefs, supporting reef fish and small marine life.
Exmouth Navy Pier is a signature Western Australian shore-access structure dive, with marine life sheltering beneath its submerged pilings.
The Rainbow Warrior is a historic shipwreck in New Zealand’s Bay of Islands region, now an artificial reef near the Cavalli Islands.
Garden Eel Cove, also called Manta Ray Heaven, is a signature Kona dive site associated with Hawaii’s manta ray night dives.
